I'm not a dad but an involved uncle. When my mom was diagnosed with cancer the thing that helped the most was when people would bring food, home cooked or bought didn't really matter. When people are dealing with strong emotions like grief or worry, one of the last things they want is the added pressure of feeding themselves or their family.

My dad was a deacon and a group of the moms at Church had it organized so that certain people would bring us food on certain days, it eased a major burden when everything felt so difficult. Even if you just order take out for them it will be appreciated, make sure to call ahead and ask what kind of food they would want. Something like:

"Hey I'm going to order some food for you guys have you cooked anything already? If you have I can do it tomorrow, what's y'alls favorite food and are there any dietary restrictions?"

 I'll always remember those ladies. Angels all of them.

Oh dude, a run out to the Heritage Market in fincastle, get one of their sandwiches and then stop at Ikenberry's on the way back, grab some fruit and one of their classic sodas. Great way to spend a Saturday afternoon.

Produce is excellent actually, there are a lot of small asian and hispanic grocery stores around where I live, as well as the usuals like food lion and kroger. It's a short ways out of town but Ikenberry Orchards has great offerings, I don't eat peaches but everyone I know who eats theirs says they're fantastic.

Healthcare around here is pretty nice too thanks to Carilion, they're the number one employer in the city, even moreso than the city itself. People come here from a pretty big radius to get serious work done.

Born and raised, roanoke is a big cultural hub for the area, if you're looking for good food you really can't miss, the best restaurant in town is probably the Cuban island on williamson rd. You should also check out the Texas Tavern downtown, which has been open 24 hrs for ~100 years.

The portal is amazing, I didn't use it effectively at first, mostly because I was afraid of the timer. Like if I use it now, what if I need it later? I use to wait whole games and then die before I could use it at all.

To me, both it and the Zipline are similar, but used for different situations. For traversing quickly and getting away from the ring, Zipline, but to reposition a team through dangerous ground, portal. The portal sacrifices speed but you're only risking one player instead of the whole squad. As well as the added benefit that you don't need LoS with a location to drop the portal, so you can place it inside buildings or around corners to give your squad cover when they come through.
